conventions.draws: Each party takes its draws in order. A `bytes` draw fills a request of exactly that length; a `u32` draw answers a request for a 32-bit integer. Host: invitation id (16), ticket secret (16), for send link the code (u32, drawn again while at least 4294000000); then for each new attempt the next code (u32, only while attempts are left after the debit) and the CPace scalar yb (32). Joiner: for each attempt the attempt id (16) and the CPace scalar ya (32). A CPace scalar is the 32 bytes with the top four bits of the last byte cleared, read little-endian.
conventions.events: host/create: create an invitation of `kind` (with `role` if given, else the conventions' role). host/grant: the host adds a grant named `name` for the joiner's identity (`role` if given, else the conventions' role; authorizing owner as for invitations; no enrollment receipt), as left by an earlier pairing. host/tick: the host's clock reaches `at`; open invitations whose time is up end. <joiner>/start: the joiner opens `ticket` that arrived by `arrival` (in_app_scan: the app's own scanner; link: anything else); `host_pinned`: it already held a pin for the ticket's host from an earlier pairing; `record`: the stored flow record for this ticket, from an earlier save; `identity: host`: the joiner uses the host's identity key. <joiner>/save: output the flow's record as stored. <joiner>/connect: a new TLS connection `conn`; both ends send HELLO, the host runs step 2 at once (a live grant: AUTHORIZED live, and the proof is answered when it arrives with PAIRED if the grant's enrollment receipt names this invitation, else a second AUTHORIZED; no grant: await the join proof, sending nothing) and the joiner sends JOIN_PROOF right after its HELLO without waiting; with `host: false` the far end is scripted. <joiner>/drop: the joiner's connection breaks with no GOAWAY either way. host/receive and <joiner>/receive: a CONTROL message arrives (checked by that end's gate first). <joiner>/goaway: the host's GOAWAY arrives. <joiner>/proof_timeout: no answer to the joiner's proof within 10 s (wire.md 8.2). <joiner>/submit_code: the owner types `code`. A receive with `crash_at_persist`: the app is killed right after the first write it asks for lands; nothing it held goes out, its flow is gone and its connection breaks. host/approve: the host owner approves the device on `conn`.
conventions.exporters: Stand-in TLS exporter values per connection. Unless `host_exporters` is given, both ends see the same session.

joiner.proof_name: `<computer> (<profile>)` (Phone (Work)) with an in-person ticket, `<computer>` (Phone) with a send link (wire.md 10.3)

conventions.outputs: send: a control message with its CONTROL frame. close: GOAWAY with its frame. attempt: the CPace inputs of a new attempt (CI is the binding transcript; sid as in wire.md). version: the minor version agreed from a HELLO. record: the joiner's flow record (canonical CBOR, wire.md 10.7; a local format). persist: the joiner asks to store `record` if the store still holds `expected` (null: nothing yet); the harness completes it at once, then the actions that waited for it follow. crashed: the app was killed. paired and already_paired are followed at once by the pin being stored, after which the joiner may clear its pending mark (persist). Others name host or joiner events: show_code, ask_approval, admitted_join_only, enrolled, invitation_ended, paired, code_rejected, failed (the joiner's flow ends with this code: its gate closes, and unless the step was a goaway or a drop, the joiner then closes the connection with GOAWAY of that code after any message listed before it in the step, wire.md 10.6 rule 9; that GOAWAY is not listed as a separate close), error, ignored.

description: End-to-end pairing (spec wire.md, sections 8, 10 and 11, and cpace.md). Each flow lists scripted random draws per party, then events in order with every output. Replaying the events with the same draws must give the same outputs byte for byte.

flows.description: In-person pairing: ticket, HELLO both ways, join proof, AUTHORIZED join-only, the owner approves, PAIRED, grant.
flows.name: in_person

flows.description: Send-link pairing: ticket, HELLO both ways, join proof, AUTHORIZED join-only, the code shown, one CPace attempt (msg_a, msg_b with the host's confirmation, msg_c with the joiner's), PAIRED, grant. The first code draw is rejected and drawn again.
flows.name: send_link

flows.description: Three wrong codes on one connection. Each attempt fails the host's confirmation on the joiner, which aborts it. A fresh code is shown at the start of attempts 1 and 2, none at attempt 3. After the third the invitation ends and the host closes with attempts_exhausted; the joiner's flow is over and refuses a fourth code.
flows.name: wrong_code_three_times

flows.description: The joiner talks to a far end that aborts every attempt. The joiner stops after its own 3 attempts and refuses a fourth code; the real host's invitation is untouched.
flows.name: joiner_cap_against_fake_host

flows.description: Joiner a holds the ticket with one bit of the secret flipped; joiner b with one bit of the invitation id flipped. The host closes both with invitation_invalid and the invitation stays open.
flows.name: tampered_tickets

flows.description: The joiner's TLS session is not the one the host sees (a relaying middle device): the join proof was made with another exporter. The host closes with invitation_invalid and the invitation stays open.
flows.name: proof_on_another_session

flows.description: The host verifies the joiner's confirmation, enrolls it and sends PAIRED, but the connection breaks before PAIRED arrives. The joiner marked its outcome pending (persist) before its confirmation went out; it reconnects with the same ticket and, as on every connection of a pairing flow, sends JOIN_PROOF right after its HELLO without waiting for the host. Step 2 finds the live grant: the host sends AUTHORIZED live at once. It then answers the proof: the grant's enrollment receipt names this invitation, so the answer is PAIRED again, with the invitation's role. The joiner takes the first live as a notice and PAIRED as its outcome: paired. Once the pin is stored it clears the pending mark (persist).
flows.name: outcome_after_lost_paired

flows.description: The device already holds an owner grant and a pin for the host. It opens a send link whose invitation would make it a client, and the code exchange runs on its live connection (the proof made it join-only). The joiner verifies the host's confirmation, marks its outcome pending (persist) and sends its own, but the connection breaks before the host reads it, so the host never enrolls it. The invitation then expires. On reconnect step 2 finds the old owner grant (AUTHORIZED live); the proof's invitation is no longer open and the grant's enrollment receipt does not name it (that grant came from elsewhere), so the answer is AUTHORIZED live, not PAIRED. The joiner reports already_paired (the device keeps the access it had; the client role is not in effect), not a completed pairing, and clears the pending mark once the pin is stored. The grant stays owner.
flows.name: role_change_not_committed

flows.description: Every write the joiner asks for (persist: a compare-and-swap of its flow record) lands before the actions that wait for it: the debit before msg_a, and the outcome-pending mark after the host's confirmation verified but before msg_c. Here the app is killed right after the pending mark lands, so msg_c never goes out and the host, seeing the connection drop, fails the attempt. Opening the link again with the stored record (2 attempts left, outcome pending) reconnects even though the flow could not know whether the host enrolled it. The host has no grant and the invitation is still open, so it admits the proof join-only: not enrolled. The joiner clears the pending mark (persist) and waits for the current code.
flows.name: crash_after_pending_mark

flows.description: PAIRED is lost as in outcome_after_lost_paired. The joiner's next connection gets no answer to its proof within 10 s (proof_timeout): it closes with not_authorized and the flow ends; it does not reconnect on its own. The stored record keeps the outcome pending, so opening the same ticket again (start with the saved record) reconnects, and the host's answer to the proof, PAIRED again for its receipt, gives the outcome.
flows.name: lost_paired_then_proof_timeout

flows.description: A send link can be swapped in transit for one that names another key; step 1 then passes against whoever holds that key, and it answers AUTHORIZED live from step 2 and AUTHORIZED live again as its answer to the proof. Joiner a has no pin for that key from before: on the answer it does not end already paired, fails with pairing_failed and pins nothing. Joiner b held a pin for the ticket's host before this flow (start with host_pinned): it ends already paired. A joiner learning the outcome of its own lost PAIRED is outcome_after_lost_paired.
flows.name: send_link_live_needs_a_pin

flows.description: The host still holds a grant for the joiner from an earlier pairing, but the joiner has lost its pin (no host_pinned). It opens a new send link. Step 2 finds the grant: the host binds the connection to it and sends AUTHORIZED live. The joiner takes that as a notice only, since it sent a proof. The proof is valid for an open invitation, so the host answers AUTHORIZED join_only (the connection is now pairing only) and shows the code. A normal code exchange follows; enrollment replaces the old grant (wire.md 7), and the connection becomes live under the new one.
flows.name: re_pair_while_granted

flows.description: A link is swapped in transit for an in-person ticket that names another key. In person skips the code, so such a ticket is accepted only from the app's own scanner. Joiner a opens it as a link: the flow is refused before dialing (in_person_from_link, reported as pairing_failed), so the far end can neither say AUTHORIZED live (already paired) nor send PAIRED after a fake approval, and nothing is pinned. Joiner b, which already holds a pin for that key, is refused the same way: the arrival decides, not the pin.
flows.name: swapped_in_person_link

flows.description: A device scans its own invitation: the ticket's host identity is its own identity. The flow is refused before dialing (own_ticket, reported as pairing_failed). A host that receives a join proof from its own identity closes with not_authorized (pairing-attempts.json, sequence join_proof_from_own_identity).
flows.name: own_ticket

flows.description: The joiner's 3 attempts are kept per ticket hash in a stored record, so neither killing the app nor opening the link again resets them. Against a far end that aborts every attempt, the joiner spends 2 attempts, saves its record and the connection drops. Opening the link again with that record leaves 1 attempt; it is spent, the flow fails with attempts_exhausted, and a further start with the saved record is refused at once.
flows.name: joiner_cap_survives_reopening
